reason: The proposed complete claim asserts the actual first end of a single power defined by Foreign Service Act1946 section411, but no actual section411 statutory text, amendment history, or statutory repeal/transition/effective-date provisions have been read. This is the specific source of the sole delegated four-class classification competence, not merely a background preamble citation. EO12292 itself identifies the 1980 Act transition and substitutes section401 of that Act for section411 in related leave authority, so statutory replacement is a concrete located lead. The EO-only and numbered-current-law searches do not resolve its timing or preservation. The original and formal revocation findings are strong; they do not by themselves establish that February15,1981 was the earliest cessation of the incorporated statutory power. No earlier end is found or invented.
findings_upheld: Complete original EO9799 read: one operative delegation directing the Secretary of State to exercise the President’s section411 authority to classify chief-of-mission positions into four classes. The exact inventory includes the effective-date sentence and excludes neighboring EOs9800/9801.

The order activates November13,1946, expressly, rather than its November8signature. No own-term sunset, reporting trigger, deadline, or one-time completion condition appears. Classifying positions is continuing delegated competence; it is not deemed spent upon an assumed first classification.

EO12292 section10(b) expressly revokes EO9799. Section11 makes the order effective as of February15,1981, rather than signatureFebruary23or publicationFebruary25. The target authority was formally withdrawn by that date; the exact original earliest-end conclusion remains unaccepted.

EO10471 delegates separate leave authority for persons compensated under section411. It does not itself amend or withdraw the classification delegation. Compensation-reference survival is not proof of unchanged classification authority.

EO10062 independently establishes a German High Commissioner position at chief-of-mission Class1. EO10608 abolishes that specific office and revokes10062/10144 under a convention-triggered effective date. Neither abolishes the Secretary of State or the general section411classification function; no target end is inferred from that office abolition.

EO10575, EO10893, EO10973 and EO12163 special-mission compensation comparisons are independent foreign-assistance functions. A comparison to chief-of-mission Class3/4 compensation, including the1979reference, does not establish the complete statutory history of section411’s four-class classification power.
EO12293 independently delegates new1980Act functions, effective February15,1981, and does not revive EO9799. Its existence does not replace reading the underlying statutory repeal and transition.

All34quoted-part occurrences,16distinct quotes, and the original inventory span match held text exactly. All10cited text hashes and official PDF fixity records match. Source-to-actor identities were checked against actual text, not copied from machine labels.
